newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major steers clear of winner's cup.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major steers clear of winner's cup.

text.p: John Major on Wednesday turned down the perfect opportunity to signal his confidence that his Conservatives would win Britain's election when he visited London's Wembley soccer stadium on the final day of campaigning.
The British prime minister was shown a replica of the F.A. Cup, the most important trophy in English club soccer, during a visit to a sporting trade fair.
Photographers who have accompanied Major over the past six weeks of camapigning implored him to lift the trophy above his head in the style of a winning captain.
But the most that Major, expected to suffer the sort of drubbing his favourite team Chelsea seldom experiences, refused.
Instead he contented himself with giving an interview to a sporting television channel in which he talked up the chances of Chelsea lifting the F.A. Cup in the final against Middlesbrough on May 17.
"They are getting towards being as great a passing side as I can remember," Major said.
He concluded his visit by having lunch with Sepp Blatter, general secretary of world soccer's governing body, FIFA.
Aides said he had pushed the case for the World Cup finals to be held in England in 2006.
